KeyHelm

KeyHelm text messages

Effective 2026-10-20

KeyHelm text messages are sent by KeyHelm LLC on behalf of landlords who use KeyHelm to run their rental homes. This page explains who sends them, what they are about, how people sign up, how often they come and how to stop them.

Who sends these texts

KeyHelm LLC ("KeyHelm") sends every text, on behalf of the landlord of the home you rent, applied for or asked about. Texts come from the landlord's KeyHelm phone number. The landlord is our customer. KeyHelm is software, not a property manager, and never collects rent.

What we text about

  • Repair updates: questions about the problem, the booked time, how to reach the vendor, and when the job is done.
  • Rent reminders before rent is due, and late notices after the landlord confirms rent hasn't arrived.
  • Showing scheduling: tour times, confirmations and door codes for self-guided tours.
  • Lease, renewal, move-in and move-out notices, including deposit statements.
  • Replies to messages you send to the landlord's KeyHelm number.
  • Home availability: only if you reply YES when we offer to text you when a home opens up.
  • For landlords who opt in: account alerts such as repair approvals and tenant updates.
  • For vendors the landlord hires: job requests and scheduling.

We never send marketing or promotional texts.

How people sign up

Tenants

The landlord adds you to KeyHelm with the mobile number you gave them for your tenancy. Our Terms only allow landlords to add people who agreed to get texts from them about the rental. Your first text is a welcome message that names KeyHelm, says what we text about and tells you how to stop (see the first sample below).

Anyone who texts first: prospects, applicants and tenants

When you text a landlord's KeyHelm number, for example about a home for rent or a repair, we reply to your message and follow up on what you asked, like tour times. Applicants also check a box on the rental application agreeing to texts and email about their application. We only text you about other homes if you reply YES when we offer.

Vendors

The landlord adds the vendors and staff they hire, with their agreement, to receive job requests by text.

Landlords (KeyHelm customers)

When you sign up on our website, the form has an optional checkbox that starts unchecked. It says:

Text me KeyHelm account alerts, like repair approvals and tenant updates. Optional, not required to buy. Message frequency varies. Msg and data rates may apply. Reply HELP for help or STOP to opt out.

You don't have to check it to buy KeyHelm. If you leave it unchecked, we email your alerts instead.

How often

Message frequency varies. It depends on what is happening with your home, like an open repair, a tour or an upcoming rent date. Notices that can wait, such as rent reminders, are held during the landlord's quiet hours (9 PM to 8 AM unless the landlord changes them).

Cost

Message and data rates may apply. KeyHelm does not charge tenants, applicants, prospects or vendors anything for texts.

Help and stopping texts

  • Reply STOP to stop texts from that number. STOPALL, UNSUBSCRIBE, CANCEL, END and QUIT work too. You'll get one text confirming it, and then no more texts. Tenants who stop texts may still get important notices about their home by email.
  • Reply START to turn texts back on.
  • Reply HELP for help. We'll reply: "KeyHelm: texts for your landlord about your rental. Help: help@keyhelm.example. Msg frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out."
  • Questions about your home, rent or lease are best answered by your landlord.

Support

Email help@keyhelm.example. KeyHelm LLC.

Your privacy

No mobile information will be shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. Text messaging opt-in data and consent are not shared with any third parties. We only use your number to send the texts described on this page. Read our Privacy policy and the "Text messaging" section of our Terms of service.

Mobile carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
